title: THC Advanced Water Quality and Irrigation
description: Advanced Water Quality and Irrigation prepares experienced controlled-environment cultivation learners to characterize source water, distinguish pH from alkalinity, verify pH/EC measurement quality, evaluate irrigation distribution, interpret root-zone moisture and dryback trends, and use water/solute mass-balance evidence to separate delivery, scheduling, source-water and accumulation problems.
intendedAudience: Cultivation Technician II and senior cultivation technicians
Staff responsible for irrigation-system verification, water-quality records, meter control or root-zone trend review
Learners progressing toward cultivation lead, irrigation or controlled-environment specialist pathways
prerequisites: THC Cultivation Foundations or equivalent plant-water/root-zone knowledge is recommended.
Learners should understand basic pH, EC, irrigation-volume and root-zone moisture terminology.
Technician I-level measurement, documentation, safety and procedure-following competency is recommended before supervised practical work.
learningOutcomes: Distinguish water pH from alkalinity and explain why repeated bicarbonate/alkalinity loading can influence root-zone behavior over time.
Build a source-water characterization plan using pH, EC, alkalinity, source history and risk-based chemistry or contaminant testing rather than one screening number.
Verify pH/EC measurement quality using device identity, calibration/verification records, standards, cleaning history and comparison checks before changing crop inputs.
Measure irrigation distribution across representative locations and interpret emitter-output variation, pressure and filtration evidence.
Interpret root-zone moisture/dryback trends in the context of substrate, container, environment, crop stage and sensor verification rather than universal dryback targets.
Evaluate irrigation timing and volume changes one variable at a time and use measured root-zone response to determine whether the change improved control.
Interpret irrigation-in, drainage/return, EC, volume and reservoir trends using a mass-balance framework.
Recognize when stable bulk EC can still hide changing ion ratios or localized root-zone accumulation.
Separate likely source-water, measurement, distribution, scheduling, root-zone and recirculation problems before recommending corrective action.
Produce a supervisor-ready irrigation/root-zone diagnostic record with measurements, uncertainty, next checks, permitted actions and escalation boundaries.
evidencePolicy: Course conclusions should rely on verified measurements, source-water records, irrigation-distribution data, root-zone trends and peer-reviewed or university/extension evidence where available. The course must distinguish screening measurements such as EC from ion-specific or contaminant testing, and must not present one pH, EC, dryback, pulse count or runoff percentage as a universal target across media, containers, cultivars, facilities or crop stages.
assessmentPolicy: Instruction uses water-analysis records, meter-verification cases, emitter catch tests, root-zone trend interpretation, scheduling scenarios and mass-balance exercises. Module checks are formative. The final credential assessment remains fail-closed until adequate bank depth, human review, accessibility review, pilot evidence and standard-setting are complete. Practical performance is demonstrated through the existing Technician II Fertigation & Root-Zone Troubleshooting practical, including measurement verification, distribution/scheduling reasoning, records and escalation.

extensions.roleBoundary: Technician II may verify measurements, execute approved procedures, evaluate irrigation distribution and root-zone trends, identify likely faults, and recommend next verification or escalation. The course does not authorize unapproved recipe changes, unrestricted chemical treatment, plumbing/electrical repair, or facility-level irrigation design outside assigned authority.
extensions.credentialStatement: Successful completion may contribute to the THC Advanced Water Quality and Irrigation certificate when all written assessment, practical, review, identity, issuance and release requirements are active. The credential documents educational/workforce achievement and is not a government license or independent personnel certification.
productionActivationRequirements: Expand and validate final-assessment bank depth across all six objectives.
Require and verify the mapped Technician II practical performance evidence.
Record human SME and assessment review.
Run learner pilot and item-analysis review.
Verify evidence-source freshness and public learner rendering.
Verify credential identity, issuance and public-verification flow.
